svg.text: Глава 13 · Стек TCP/IP. Адресация
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0365:c01–p0398:c01 · PDF 365–398 · printed 364–397
1 · TCP/IP architecture
Application → services/protocols used by programs
Transport → TCP reliable stream or UDP datagram service
Internet/network → IP packet forwarding across heterogeneous subnetworks
Network-interface → local technology carries IP to the next directly connected node
IP packet persists logically; link frame is replaced at each router hop
2 · IPv4 identity and prefixes
IPv4 → 32-bit network-layer address
Mask/prefix → network bits vs host/address-pool bits
Private/public scopes → different uniqueness requirements
CIDR → contiguous prefix-based pools sized closer to demand
Classful A/B/C/D/E is historical source context, not the operational default model
3 · ARP: next-hop local delivery
Routing/on-link logic yields next-hop IPv4 address
ARP cache hit → reuse local/MAC mapping
Cache miss → broadcast ARP request on local broadcast domain
Matching interface replies → mapping cached dynamically
Static entry → administrator-created; source names arp utility, no syntax
Proxy-ARP answers on behalf of a remote node; RARP is a separate reverse-mapping mechanism
4 · DNS: scalable naming
Hierarchical domain tree delegates administrative responsibility
Resolver → local/client-side API; DNS server → distributed mapping database
Zone → authoritative records; cache → non-authoritative learned answers
Iterative / recursive / mixed lookup procedures
Reverse IPv4 naming → reversed octets under in-addr.arpa
Forward and reverse datasets can diverge because they are maintained separately
5 · DHCP: scalable configuration
Server manages address pool + lease duration
Client starts with local broadcast discovery
Server(s) offer → client requests one → selected server acknowledges
Relay forwards requests to a DHCP server in another subnet
Dynamic addresses complicate stable DNS identity, monitoring and IP-based filters
6 · Diagnostic dependency chain
Wrong IP/prefix → wrong on-link/routed decision
Wrong/missing ARP → cannot build local frame to next hop
DNS failure → name unavailable even if IP path is healthy
DHCP failure → host may never receive usable IP/prefix/gateway/DNS state
Separate these layers before changing configuration
Operational reading rule
Addressing incident → capture IP/prefix/gateway/DNS → next-hop decision → ARP → IP path → DNS → DHCP lease source.
Do not jump from “name does not resolve” directly to routing changes, or from “ARP missing” directly to DNS changes.
No concrete vendor/OS command syntax is supplied by the chapter.
Chapter 14 starts at p0399:c01 · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
